Hi Alex / Priya

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate performance in a Private/VPC deployment: 

1) Target SLOs you mentioned: end-to-end p95 latency <= 200ms for short responses (<=512 tokens) and streaming p95 for chunk delivery <= 150ms. Please confirm if these are firm targets or goals.
2) Expected concurrency/throughput: you indicated ~25 concurrent peers at peak with ~60 requests/sec sustained during business hours, spiking to ~120 req/sec for short windows.
3) Network topology: you are planning to peer via AWS Transit Gateway from the us-east-1 VPC to Redwood private endpoints, with a site-to-site VPN fallback.
4) Next tests: Jordan will provide the test plan + expected packet/connection details. We need your network team to run a traceroute and provide egress IPs and firewall rules.

Attached: initial test plan (draft) and a stub for traceroute instructions.

Action items: 
- Alex: share traceroute output and any existing internal latency budgets.
- Netops: provide egress/NAT IP ranges and whether you will allow static routing to Redwood endpoints.
- Jordan: will send an e2e test plan and sample traffic profile tomorrow.

If anything above is off, flag it and I'll update. We can schedule the connectivity test once we have the traceroute and the firewall rules.

Hi Alex / Priya

Following up with more concrete numbers and what we need from your side to validate the SLOs in a Private/VPC deployment. High level notes: 

- Redwood internal inference: for our reference model in dedicated/private mode, pure model token generation time is ~25-40ms p95 on the shard (depending on model quantization).
- Network add: to meet end-to-end p95 <=200ms for 512-token responses (non-streaming), the customer-side network budget should be <=120ms p95 round-trip from the application to the Redwood egress (this includes VPN/peering hop + intra-cloud routing). That gives ~80ms headroom for model + service processing.
- Streaming: for chunked streaming (we recommend 200-500ms chunk cadence), aim for p95 chunk delivery <=150ms. This is highly sensitive to packet loss; please keep MTU standard and avoid additional NAT layers if possible.
- Concurrency/throughput sizing: your stated 25 concurrent clients and 60 req/s sustained is modest. For validation we recommend a test profile of 100 concurrent connections ramped to 150 req/s for 10 minutes to observe queuing/backpressure. Jordan: we will run a canary with 3 model workers to emulate load.

What we need from ACME network team: 
- Traceroute and mtr to the Redwood private endpoint from at least 2 app subnets (attach results).
- Egress/NAT IP ranges or confirmation that you can whitelist static Redwood egress IP set.
- Whether peering is via AWS TGW or direct VPC peering, and if there are intermediaries (firewalls, proxies) that may terminate TLS.
- Any internal latency budgets (app->service) you are already tracking.

I attached a short test plan (redwood-e2e-test-plan.pdf) with endpoints, ports, and a sample traffic profile. Once we have traceroutes and egress IPs, we can provision a temporary test ACL and kick off the canary.

If it helps, we can also provide a small k8s job you can run that streams test payloads from your side and reports chunk latencies back to us for diagnosis.

-Jordan

Thanks Marissa/Jordan, looping in our NetOps team. Per your ask, attached is a traceroute from our primary app subnet (app-us-east-1a) to the Redwood endpoint and a short network topology diagram. A few notes from NetOps: 

- We are peering via AWS Transit Gateway; traffic egresses through a pair of NAT gateways in the shared-services account. Egress IPs: 54.210.33.12, 54.210.33.13 (these are the NATs we would expect to whitelist).
- The TGW path adds ~12-18ms average RTT to external endpoints historically; we'll attach the raw mtr.
- We can set up a direct VPC peer if that materially improves latency, but that requires change window and security approvals.

- Internal latency budgets: our application team targets <=80ms app->external service p95. Combining that with your 120ms network budget is tight but possibly workable if we remove an extra NAT hop.

Attaching: acme-traceroute-20270621.txt, network-topology.png
